The proposed solution claims that the maximum weight for which $\mathbb{F}_q$-linear independence holds is $w_{\max} = q - 1$, and that the first $\mathbb{F}_q$-linear relation occurs at weight $w = q$ involving $\zeta(q)$ and depth-$2$ values like $\zeta(q - 1, 1)$.

This is incorrect:
1. For any depth $r \ge 2$, an MZV $\zeta(s_1, \ldots, s_r) = \sum_{d_1 > \dots > d_r \ge 0} S_{d_1}(s_1) \cdots S_{d_r}(s_r)$ has $d_1 \ge 1$, so every term has strictly positive $\infty$-adic valuation ($v_\infty > 0$).
2. In contrast, the depth-$1$ value $\zeta(q) = \sum_{d \ge 0} S_d(q) = 1 + S_1(q) + \cdots$ has $v_\infty(\zeta(q)) = 0$.
3. Therefore, no non-trivial $\mathbb{F}_q$-linear relation at weight $q$ can involve $\zeta(q)$. For instance, when $q = 2$, the only weight-$2$ MZVs are $\zeta(2)$ (with valuation $0$) and $\zeta(1, 1)$ (with valuation $2$), which are strictly linearly independent over $\mathbb{F}_2$. Linear independence at weight $q$ holds.

VERDICT: REJECT
